page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8581C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz and is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The instance is configured with 60.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-16 demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2269.0 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 35.06 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is solid, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14602.98 and a Passmark CPU score of 23179.01. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only large block bandwidth of 109.68 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 50.45 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the instance processes text efficiently, scoring in the top tier for Geekbench text processing, and handles small-model LLM text generation at a strong rate of 330.39 tokens/sec.

Given its dedicated hardware allocation and balanced resource density, the c4-standard-16 offers a reliable performance-to-resource ratio for workloads requiring consistent CPU execution without the overhead of local storage or GPU accelerators. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing for customizable block storage attachments. This configuration is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate-scale text or language model inference tasks.
